title: He saves the positive
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: When something hits you hard, what do you hold on to?
In class, Jose read what the author wrote after losing his father.
I also knew that he wouldn't have wanted me to spend time grieving.

The author went on to say that his father's company was his father's life work, that he loved it, and that what he wanted most was for it to be saved. Those are very big statements, Jose said. It shows that mentally he took himself to a positive place.
But let's think for a second, he said. What would have happened if he had gone to a negative place? What are the negatives he could have gone into?

He was twenty-four. His father had said he was too young to take a big role. So what support system does he have, Jose asked? A student said: he doesn't. He just has himself, and the principles he learned from his dad.
Jose agreed. That's it. He only has himself, and the biggest influence in his entire life is now gone.
Jose asked: what in his childhood contributed to that confidence? A student said: all the times he was on his own at school and had to figure it out.
Jose added that the father put him in positions where he had to adapt on his own. So the father created an independent person.
He saves the positive of what the father wanted to do, Jose said, not the negative. He uses that as his mental positive anchor to continue. That is really critical.
The author says he was a nervous wreck and his head was spinning. Jose said he is very aware of the challenges and of his emotional state, but he doesn't let himself brood in it and stay in it.
In times of massive pressure, he said, he is going to show up. Those are decisions we make in our life. You can look at pressure in many ways.
What would you save from a hard moment: the positive or the negative?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write one hard thing that has happened to you, in one line.
Write the negative story you could tell yourself about it.
Write one positive thing you can keep from it, something someone you care about would have wanted for you.
Write that as one sentence, your anchor.
Write the first small action you can take from that anchor today.

check.q: What did Jose call the positive thing the author kept from his father?
What did a student say about the author's support system?
choices: He had only himself and his father's principles

check.q: What did Jose say the author did not do with his emotions?
choices: Let himself brood in them and stay in them

recap: Under pressure, save the positive and use it as your anchor.
